passage:
On the colony ground, Naveen and Vandana were the captains for the cricket match. Naveen chose first. “Aryan!” Aryan, the best batter, jumped up grinning. Vandana chose next. “Meera, she's our fastest fielder.” They went back and forth, and Naveen felt tall and proud, like a king. The circle shrank. Only Tanay was left, hands in pockets, looking at his shoes.

Naveen noticed. He remembered the day Tanay had caught three balls at the fence. “Tanay, you're my wicketkeeper,” he said. Tanay's shoulders lifted. Vandana muttered, “We didn't have a keeper anyway.” Naveen grinned. “Now we do.”

qa.q: What was Naveen feeling when choosing first?
qa.a: Naveen felt tall and proud, like a king, at having the first pick.

qa.q: What choice did Naveen make about Tanay, and why?
qa.a: Naveen remembered Tanay's three catches at the fence and chose Tanay as wicketkeeper, giving the team a strength it lacked.

qa.q: How might Tanay have felt standing with hands in pockets and then hearing a name called?
qa.a: Tanay probably felt anxious and small while waiting, then relieved and proud to be picked for a real role.

grounding: A child choosing sides feels the pride of first pick, and learns that a team needs different strengths.

passage:
“Rock, paper, scissors for first pick,” Swati said. “I won. Meher.”

“Fine. Zoya,” said Jahnavi.

“Aditya.”

“Priya. She's fast.”

Swati grinned. “Ooh, we'll beat you.” Then she glanced around. Only three children were left: Kabir, Ritu and little Sunil, who studied the ground.

“You go,” Jahnavi whispered. “We can't pick only the fast ones.”

“Kabir's slow.”

“He keeps score best. Ritu remembers all the rules. And Sunil throws well when nobody's watching.”

Swati paused. “Okay. Kabir, you keep score. Ritu, you hold the whistle. Sunil, you throw first.”

Sunil looked up quickly. “Really?”

“Really,” said Swati, and meant it.

qa.q: How did the captains decide who picks first?
qa.a: They played rock, paper, scissors, and Swati won.

qa.q: Why did Sunil look up quickly and ask, “Really?”
qa.a: Sunil was surprised and hopeful, having expected to be picked last and hardly believing being given a real job.

qa.q: What did Swati change after Jahnavi whispered about the remaining children?
qa.a: Swati stopped choosing only the fastest and gave Kabir, Ritu and Sunil roles that used their strengths.

qa.q: How might Jahnavi see what a team needs?
qa.a: Jahnavi sees that a team needs different strengths, like scorekeeping, rule-keeping and throwing, not just speed.

grounding: Children choosing sides feel the pride of being picked first, and learn that a team needs different strengths.
